competitive_landscape: The water is used mostly for dhow tours and Corniche leisure cruises, with water-taxi service at The Pearl and Lusail. There is no commuter or premium point-to-point network across the inner bay, and no fast sea link to Gulf neighbours despite the short crossing distances. Doha's purpose-built waterfront is an open canvas.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves an at-scale clean marine network is bankable and deliverable on a multi-year phasing.

regulatory_note: Marine transport falls under the Ministry of Transport and Mwani Qatar (ports), within a Qatar-National-Vision-2030 clean-mobility frame — a fit for a designed-in zero-emission marine layer.
seasonality: The inner bay is sheltered and operable year-round; summer (Jun–Sep) is intensely hot but calm, winter (Oct–Apr) is the peak season with occasional shamal chop. Major-event seasons (sport, conference) spike premium demand.

summary: Doha pairs a dense, master-planned inner waterfront — the Corniche, West Bay, The Pearl, Lusail and Katara — with an open-Gulf position that puts Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Manama and the Saudi coast within a single hybrid leg. The inner waters are made for all-electric hops; the Gulf is made for long-range hybrids.
tagline: A purpose-built waterfront capital with a Gulf full of single-leg corridors.
transit_planning: For an authority: Navier adds a premium, zero-emission marine layer across the master-planned waterfront and a credible Gulf inter-city corridor — additive to existing transport, with surge capacity for the event calendar.
